item.text: {"question_id":"4B.2","answer":"No. During the relevant 2023 period, the evidence indicates that Sisi’s government used institutional design and state powers in ways that entrenched his rule, although the supplied material does not establish his personal direction of every enforcement action. The 2019 constitutional amendments extended his possible tenure to 2030, increased presidential control over the judiciary, and expanded the military’s political and judicial authority; emergency-style restrictions were also permanently codified after the state of emergency ended (BATCH-0006-E015; BATCH-0009-R01-E008; BATCH-0009-R02-E013). The UN Human Rights Committee further found that presidential appointment authority over judicial bodies and the prosecutor compromised judicial independence, while politically motivated cases and prolonged pretrial detention affected critics and opponents (BATCH-0011-E016). In 2023, the election administration obstructed or failed to remedy opposition endorsement efforts, security and prosecutorial authorities detained or prosecuted Tantawy supporters and other critics, and Amnesty reported government involvement in spyware targeting of Tantawy’s phone (BATCH-0008-E018; BATCH-0009-R03-E004; BATCH-0009-R03-E009; BATCH-0020-E005). Broader assessments describe policymaking as dominated by the military and intelligence agencies, parliament as largely a pro-regime rubber stamp, and media and public information as under strict state control (BATCH-0008-E001; BATCH-0008-E010; BATCH-0002-E005). Sisi’s national-dialogue and democratic-government statements, the formal constitutional framework, the end of the state of emergency, prisoner releases, and the pardon of Patrick Zaki provide contrary or qualifying evidence of stated pluralism or individual corrective action, but the supplied evidence does not show that these measures dismantled the institutional entrenchment pattern (BATCH-0019-E005; BATCH-0021-E014; BATCH-0024-R01-E004; BATCH-0009-R03-E002; BATCH-0009-R03-E010; BATCH-0008-E027).","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0006-E015","BATCH-0009-R01-E008","BATCH-0009-R02-E013","BATCH-0011-E016","BATCH-0008-E018","BATCH-0009-R03-E004","BATCH-0009-R03-E009","BATCH-0020-E005","BATCH-0008-E001","BATCH-0008-E010","BATCH-0002-E005"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0019-E005","BATCH-0021-E014","BATCH-0024-R01-E004","BATCH-0009-R03-E002","BATCH-0009-R03-E010","BATCH-0008-E027"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The evidence strongly supports institutional and governmental entrenchment but does not establish Sisi’s personal order or knowledge for every arrest, prosecution, election-administration failure, media restriction, or surveillance incident.","Some favorable evidence consists of official statements or formal rules and does not establish implementation, practical independence, or genuine contestability.","The evidence supports individual pardons and releases, but does not show broader institutional correction of the underlying legal or coercive practices.","Some reported institutional changes predate 2023; they are included because the supplied evidence states that they remained operative during 2023 or directly shaped Sisi’s continued tenure."] ,"corrections_made":["Added the omitted evidence on permanent codification of emergency-style powers and presidential control over judicial appointments.","Reframed the releases and Zaki pardon as limited individual corrective actions rather than evidence of institutional non-entrenchment.","Removed any implication that every adverse act was personally directed by Sisi.","Preserved formal democratic commitments and constitutional provisions as qualifying evidence while distinguishing them from implementation and de facto practice.","Kept the conclusion period-specific to the 2023 context and did not score the answer."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Reopen if additional evidence materially changes the attribution of election, judicial, security, media, or surveillance actions to Sisi personally rather than to state institutions under his presidency.","Reopen if evidence demonstrates that the constitutional, judicial, emergency-law, or election-administration arrangements were substantially corrected during the target period."]}
